newsitem.title: PERU: Mexico's Penoles takes 60 pct of Peru's La Oroya.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Penoles takes 60 pct of Peru's La Oroya.

text.p: Mexico's Industrias Penoles SA agreed Monday to acquire 60 percent of Peru's La Oroya metallurgic complex, state miner Centromin said.
Penoles agreed to pay the government $33.98 million and inject $192.55 million as fresh capital into a mixed company managing the asset, Centromin said in a statement.
Centromin will keep a 40 percent stake, of which La Oroya's workers have the right to buy a 10 percent package.

Penoles, Mexico's largest silver and gold producer, won last month the right to acquire a majority share in La Oroya at an auction. Under the terms of the sale Penoles is also obliged to invest $135 million in the La Oroya company over the next five years, Centromin said.
This investment "guarantees the modernization and expansion process that the La Oroya metallurgic complex needs so much," the statement said.

La Oroya lies in the country's central Andes 12,300 feet (3,700 meters) above sea level and 120 miles (190 km) east of Lima. The complex of refineries and smelters processes 22 metals and their byproducts.
Penoles has said it is interested in bidding at Centromin's next auction mid-July for the mining unit Mahr Tunel.
Centromin's asset sales are part of its ongoing, piecemeal privatization, which is set to continue with the auction of more mines, hydroelectric plants and polymetallic mineral deposits.
